name: i.MX 6ULL MPU interrupt fabric
summary: Application-processor architecture with executable single-candidate GIC forwarding gates and priority-mask comparison. CPU, cache/MMU, DRAM, power, and peripheral subsystems remain documented architectural boundaries.

groups.label: Generic Interrupt Controller
groups.description: One eligible candidate and one CPU interface. This does not implement the whole GIC arbitration/state machine.

groups.label: Distributor and target
groups.description: Pending state, per-interrupt enable, group forwarding, and CPU target selection.

groups.label: CPU interface and priority
groups.description: CPU-interface enable and effective priority-mask comparison. Remaining preemption/security qualifications are external.

groups.label: Application CPU complex
groups.description: Cortex-A7 and cache/MMU context, distinct from the MCU-oriented Cortex-M example.

groups.label: Memory subsystem
groups.description: External-memory controller, system DRAM, and on-chip SRAM context.

groups.label: Peripheral and security fabric
groups.description: AIPS peripherals, DMA/I/O, and i.MX 6ULL-specific security context.

groups.label: Clock and low-power control
groups.description: GPC wakeup and clock/power management remain outside the executable GIC slice.

inputs.label: Candidate pending
inputs.description: A pending interrupt candidate supplied by the surrounding GIC state. Edge capture and pending storage are not simulated.

inputs.label: Targets CPU 0
inputs.description: The candidate's effective target includes this CPU interface.

inputs.label: Distributor forwarding
inputs.description: Effective forwarding enable for the represented interrupt group.

inputs.label: CPU interface enabled
inputs.description: Effective CPU-interface signaling enable for the represented interrupt group.

inputs.label: Other GIC checks pass
inputs.description: External contract input covering running/group priority, active state, security grouping, and candidate selection. The model cannot derive these from the pending bit alone.

inputs.label: Effective IRQ priority
inputs.description: Effective read-back priority code after implementation-specific unimplemented-bit handling. Lower numeric values mean higher priority.

inputs.label: Effective priority mask
inputs.description: Only a numerically lower candidate priority passes. Equality is blocked, not X.

blocks.label: Enabled pending candidate
blocks.description: Per-interrupt enable and pending status must both be present.

blocks.label: Distributor forwarding
blocks.description: Forward this candidate only when the target CPU and distributor gate permit it.

blocks.label: Priority mask check
blocks.description: A digital less-than comparison: IRQ priority must be strictly higher, meaning numerically lower, than PMR.

blocks.label: CPU signaling eligibility
blocks.description: The represented candidate may be signaled under the supplied GIC qualifications. This does not execute an interrupt acknowledge or enter a CPU exception.

blocks.label: Cortex-A7 application CPU
blocks.description: The i.MX 6ULL has one Arm Cortex-A7 application core.
blocks.reason: No instruction execution, exception entry, operating system, or pipeline is emulated.

blocks.label: Cache and MMU context
blocks.description: Cache and virtual-memory context of the application processor. The public product page specifies 128 KB L2.
blocks.reason: No cache hits, page-table walks, translations, or coherency transactions are generated.

blocks.label: External-memory controller
blocks.description: The processor supports a 16-bit LPDDR2 / DDR3 / DDR3L interface.
blocks.reason: No controller initialization, DRAM protocol, timing, or bandwidth model is provided.

blocks.label: Board DRAM
blocks.description: Board-provided external memory, not embedded Flash as on the MCU example.
blocks.reason: Size and memory part are unspecified because no board has been selected.

blocks.label: On-chip SRAM
blocks.description: On-chip SRAM appears in the NXP BSP memory map; reserved portions depend on firmware and power-management use.
blocks.reason: No SRAM contents, reserved-region policy, or physical floorplan is inferred from the device tree.

blocks.label: AIPS peripheral fabric
blocks.description: BSP AIPS buses host serial I/O, timers, display, and other peripheral register ranges.
blocks.reason: Device-tree hierarchy is not a transistor-level interconnect netlist. No bus transaction is executed.

blocks.label: GPIO / UART / DMA / display
blocks.description: Representative peripheral functions of the applications processor; pin/package/board configuration is separate.
blocks.reason: No peripheral engines, DMA transfers, framebuffers, or pin multiplexing are simulated.

blocks.label: DCP and security context
blocks.description: The i.MX 6ULL BSP removes the i.MX 6UL CAAM node and adds DCP/RNGB context; the two variants must not be conflated.
blocks.reason: No cryptography, secure boot, security policy, or isolation guarantee is simulated.

blocks.label: General power controller
blocks.description: The NXP BSP routes wakeup/interrupt context through GPC toward the GIC.
blocks.reason: Wakeup routing, retention, low-power transitions, and clock domains are not executed.

connections.label: Application memory hierarchy
connections.description: Logical CPU/cache relationship, not a physical placement claim.

connections.label: External memory accesses
connections.description: Aggregated architectural path with unspecified internal fabric.

connections.label: Board memory interface
connections.description: Physical board memory model and package wiring are not supplied.

connections.label: Peripheral bus context
connections.description: Aggregated peripheral group from the product/BSP descriptions.

connections.label: Security register context
connections.description: DCP/RNGB nodes from the 6ULL-specific BSP description.

connections.label: Wakeup/interrupt context
connections.description: Structural relationship from the inherited interrupt-parent hierarchy.

connections.label: GIC pending boundary
connections.description: Does not synthesize a pending bit; pending remains an external snapshot input.

connections.label: CPU signaling boundary
connections.description: No IAR acknowledge, EOI, or exception entry is inferred.

outputs.label: CPU signaling eligible
outputs.description: Under the explicitly supplied other GIC qualifications.

requirements.text: Pending, per-interrupt enable, target selection, and distributor enable all gate forwarding.
Only an effective numeric priority strictly below the effective PMR value passes; equality blocks.
CPU-interface enable and all external preemption/security qualifications remain necessary for eligibility.

assumptions: One candidate is considered; other_checks represents all otherwise-unmodeled active/running priority, security, and arbitration decisions.
Priority inputs are effective unsigned read-back values after implementation-specific priority-bit handling; arbitrary writes are not emulated.
MPU denotes microprocessor/application processor here, not Arm's Memory Protection Unit acronym.
Architectural relationships are logical product/BSP descriptions. They are not physical netlists or executed memory traffic.
omissions: Complete GIC active/pending state, IAR/EOIR side effects, security groups, running priority, CPU exception entry, and OS behavior.
Instruction execution, caches, MMU/page tables, DDR timing, DMA, power management, and peripheral protocols.
No exact package, speed grade, board memory size, physical placement, electrical timing, or full-chip conformance claim.
